2609.03814.title: Evaluating Criterion-Conditioned Behaviour of Large Language Models in Content Moderation
2609.03814.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong performance on standard content moderation benchmarks. However, these benchmarks often aggregate multiple moderation criteria into a single label, making it unclear whether models can disentangle them and reliably apply each criterion when making decisions. To study whether LLMs exhibit criterion-conditioned behaviour, we introduce Diagnostic Evaluation of COntent (DECO), a criterion-independent factorisation of content that enables controlled, criterion-level evaluation. We also introduce pairwise evaluation to compare model outputs across different criteria for the same input. Across four moderation datasets and four LLMs, we find that strong benchmark performance can hide substantial failures at the criterion level. Models struggle most when correct decisions depend not on overall harmfulness, but on the specific aspect of the content that the criterion requires them to assess. Our results highlight a key limitation of current content moderation benchmarks: strong performance on aggregated labels does not provide sufficient evidence that LLMs can reliably evaluate content with respect to individual moderation criteria. These findings call for the development of evaluation methods that explicitly measure criterion-conditioned behaviour.
2609.03814.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在標準內容審核基準上表現出色。<lb/>然而，這些基準通常將多個審核標準聚合為一個單一標籤，這使得不清楚模型是否能夠將它們分開並在做出決策時可靠地應用每個標準。<lb/>為了研究LLMs是否表現出標準條件的行為，我們引入了內容的診斷評估（DECO），這是一種與標準無關的內容因子分解，能夠進行控制的標準級評估。<lb/>我們還引入了成對評估，以比較相同輸入下不同標準的模型輸出。<lb/>在四個審核數據集和四個LLMs中，我們發現強大的基準表現可能掩蓋了在標準層面上的重大失敗。<lb/>當正確的決策不依賴於整體的有害性，而依賴於標準要求評估的內容特定方面時，模型最難以應對。<lb/>我們的結果突顯了當前內容審核基準的一個關鍵局限性：在聚合標籤上的強大表現並不能提供充分的證據來證明LLMs能夠可靠地根據個別審核標準評估內容。<lb/>這些發現呼籲開發明確測量標準條件行為的評估方法。
